newsitem.title: SYRIA: Radical Palestinian urges uprising against Israel.
newsitem.headline: Radical Palestinian urges uprising against Israel.

text.p: A radical Palestinian leader on Friday pledged more attacks on Israelis and urged Palestinians to launch a fresh uprising against the Jewish state.

George Habash, the 71-year-old leader of the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine (PFLP), also said a new political alliance would be formed in the West Bank and Gaza very soon to wreck the Palestinian-Israeli peace deal.
On Thursday the PFLP, which has strong support in the West Bank and Gaza Strip, claimed responsibility for Wednesday's killing of a Jewish settler and her 12-year-old son in the West Bank.

Habash's statements came as the Israeli army said Katyusha rockets slammed into the Western Galilee region of northern Israel. The rocket salvo was the first such attack against northern Israel since a U.S. brokered ceasefire ended a 17-day Israeli blitz in April against pro-Iranian Hizbollah guerrillas based in south Lebanon.
Habash, addressing a fully packed hall at the Palestinian Yarmouk refugee camp near Damascus on the 29th anniversary of the group's founding, praised Syria's "steadfastness against Israel".
PFLP members interrupted Habash's speech several times to chant slogans praising those who died while carrying out attacks against Israel.

"With out blood and souls we redeem the martyrs," they chanted in the hall decorated with Palestinian flags and pictures of PFLP guerrillas who died in suicide attacks against Israel. There were about 1,500 people at the rally, also attended by representatives of Syria, Lebanese parties and Cuba.
In his speech Habash said the fight against Israel would continue.

"We pledge to our martyrs that we will continue our operations and military struggle against Israel until we succeed in establishing an independent Palestinian state with Jerusalem as its capital," Habash said.
His group has claimed responsibility for numerous attacks against Israelis in Israel and south Lebanon in recent years.

Habash strongly condemned Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and said his approval for building more settlements in the Israeli-occupied areas constituted a declaration of war against Palestinians.

"The increase of Israel's repressive measures against our Palestinian people and the expansion of settlements require our masses in the occupied homeland to renew their intifada (uprising) against Israel," he said.
Habash repeated his opposition to the 1993 PLO-Israeli peace deal that gave Palestinians limited self-rule in parts of the West Bank and Gaza Strip.
"The agreements, which did not respond to the minimum Palestinian rights, have created the climate for more resistance operations against Israel," Habash said.
Netanyahu has angered Arabs by delaying implementation of parts of the PLO-Israeli deals and lifting a freeze on settlement building that was imposed by the former Israeli cabinet.
Habash's group is part of a 10-member radical Palestinian alliance opposed to peace with Israel.
Islamic members of the alliance claimed responsibility for a wave of suicide bombings in Israel after the signing of the peace accord in which scores of people were killed.
